Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like early 2014. Unemployment is 6.7%, which matches December 2013 or January 2014 (6.6% in January). The 10-year yield is 2.73% and the fed funds rate is 0.08%. Gold fell about 20% over 12 months, consistent with a snapshot near the end of January 2014. US equities returned 22.3% over 12 months, which also fits.

Payrolls averaged 129k over the 3 months. That is low because the December 2013 payroll gain was only 75k. With the unemployment rate at 6.7%, the snapshot is probably December 2013 data, published in January 2014, though possibly the January 2014 report.

The 10-year yield was about 3.0% at the end of December 2013 and about 2.65% at the end of January 2014. The 3-month change of -0.31 means the yield was about 3.04 three months earlier, which fits an end-January 2014 reading of roughly 2.73. At the end of October 2013 it was about 2.55, and the end-of-November reading was 2.75, so the data points to a different month than I first read.

Checking the 20y+ Treasury 3-month return of +7.7%, which fits a window to the end of January 2014. The 1-month emerging-market return of +3.9% does not fit January 2014, when emerging markets fell. The month could instead be February 2014, when emerging markets rebounded, gold rose, and the 10-year yield was about 2.65%. But gold's 1-month return is -3.1%, which does not fit February.

The 3-month return of +2.7% for the 7-10y Treasury and the 1-month return of -0.6% are consistent with the yield rising during the month. The unemployment rate of 6.7% fits November 2013, when it was 7.0%, only loosely. Revisions to the data may account for the gap. Gold falling 3.1% fits December 2013 (-3.6%). The 10-year yield was 2.75% at the end of November 2013 and 3.04% at the end of December 2013. I am therefore leaning toward a month with a yield near 2.73%.

The 12-month change in the 10-year yield of +0.86 implies a year-earlier yield of about 1.87, which matches the end of February 2013 or the end of March 2013. That fits an end-of-February 2014 snapshot. The 3-month change of -0.31 implies about 3.04 at the end of November 2013 or December 2013. This is consistent with a March 2014 date or a February 2014 date. Emerging-market equities gained 3.3% in February 2014, and gold gained about 6.6% that month, which contradicts the data. In March 2014 the 10-year yield was 2.72% at month-end, which matches the 2.73 reading. Gold fell 3.1% in March 2014 (from 1327 to 1284), and emerging markets rose about 3 to 4%. Unemployment was 6.7% in March 2014, which matches. The 3-month average of payrolls was about 129k. March 2014 therefore fits.
